sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: CLOSED UPPER LOW NEAR THE FOUR CORNERS AREA WILL MOVE SLOWLY EAST... REACHING THE CNTRL AND SRN HIGH PLAINS THURSDAY NIGHT. A DRYLINE/LEE TROUGH WILL PERSIST OVER THE HIGH PLAINS IN ADVANCE OF THIS FEATURE. THE DRYLINE WILL MIX ACROSS WRN TX DURING THE DAY THEN RETREAT WWD DURING THE EVENING BEFORE IT IS OVERTAKEN BY A PACIFIC FRONT.

sections.title: CNTRL AND SRN HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: RECENT OBSERVATIONS INDICATE THE RICHER BOUNDARY LAYER MOISTURE WITH DEWPOINTS IN THE LOW 60S IS CONFINED TO SRN TX. ELY LOW LEVEL TRAJECTORIES RESULTING FROM THE CIRCULATION AROUND CP HIGH PRESSURE ANCHORED OVER THE ERN U.S. WILL LIMIT NWD EXTENT OF QUALITY MOISTURE RETURN WITH 60S LIKELY REMAINING ACROSS SOUTH OR SCNTRL TX. MODELS INDICATE AN INCREASE IN ELEVATED/MID LEVEL CONVECTION WILL DEVELOP EARLY THURSDAY OVER PORTIONS OF THE SRN PLAINS AS IMPULSE CURRENTLY MOVING THROUGH NRN MEXICO CONTINUES ENEWD. THIS ACTIVITY MAY BE CAPABLE OF PRODUCING MARGINALLY SEVERE HAIL. IN WAKE OF THE MORNING CONVECTION...ANY LOW CLOUDS WILL LIKELY MIX OUT FROM WRN TX THROUGH THE CNTRL HIGH PLAINS. DIABATIC HEATING BENEATH STEEP MID LEVEL LAPSE RATES WILL CONTRIBUTE TO DESTABILIZATION IN THIS REGION WITH AN AXIS OF MLCAPE RANGING FROM AROUND 1500 J/KG OVER THE TRANSPECOS REGION OF WRN TX TO 500 J/KG FARTHER NORTH INTO ERN CO WHERE MOISTURE WILL BE MORE LIMITED. SURFACE BASED THUNDERSTORMS WILL BECOME INCREASINGLY PROBABLE IN THIS REGION BY MID-LATE AFTERNOON AS THE ATMOSPHERE DESTABILIZES AND CAP WEAKENS. sections.title: CENTRAL/SOUTHERN HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: EARLY MORNING SURFACE ANALYSIS/12Z OBSERVED RAOBS DEPICT A WEST-NORTHWESTWARD RETURN OF MODEST BOUNDARY LAYER MOISTURE ACROSS TX SINCE LAST EVENING...ALTHOUGH 60+ F SURFACE DEWPOINTS ARE CONFINED TO THE TX HILL COUNTRY/SOUTH TX AS OF 13Z. INITIALLY...ON THE EASTERN PERIPHERY OF A STRONG ELEVATED MIXED LAYER SAMPLED BY 12Z REGIONAL RAOBS SUCH AS AMA/MAF/DRT/DDC...THERE IS SOME POTENTIAL FOR EARLY DAY TSTMS TO POSE A HAIL RISK ACROSS PORTIONS OF CENTRAL TX/HILL COUNTRY OWING TO A LEAD MID LEVEL IMPULSE CROSSING FAR NORTHERN MEXICO EARLY THIS MORNING. WITH IMPLIED LIFT/MID LEVEL MOISTENING NOTED EARLY THIS MORNING ACROSS THE TX HILL COUNTRY...A CONDITIONAL SURFACE BASED SEVERE THREAT COULD EVOLVE WITHIN THIS CORRIDOR...ALTHOUGH THE STRENGTH OF THE CAP /PER 12Z DRT RAOB/ SHOULD LIMIT APPRECIABLE SURFACE BASED DEVELOPMENT. sections.title: NEB/KS/OK EARLY AFTERNOON
sections.text: A NARROW CORRIDOR OF ELEVATED THUNDERSTORMS HAS DEVELOPED THIS MORNING FROM WESTERN NORTH TX INTO PARTS OF NORTHWEST KS/SOUTHEAST NEB. THIS ACTIVITY IS IN REGION OF LOW LEVEL WARM/MOIST ADVECTION AND LIFT...ALONG WITH SUFFICIENT MUCAPE. A FEW STORMS MAY PRODUCE HAIL THROUGH MID AFTERNOON...BUT ORGANIZED SEVERE ACTIVITY IS NOT ANTICIPATED. REFER TO SWOMCD NUMBER 481 FOR FURTHER DETAILS.

sections.title: EASTERN CO THIS AFTERNOON
sections.text: SOUTHEASTERLY LOW LEVEL WINDS ACROSS EASTERN CO ARE HELPING TO SLOWLY ADVECT MOISTURE INTO REGION. PRIMARY DRYLINE WILL LIKELY DEVELOP OVER FAR EASTERN CO...BUT BACKED WINDS NEAR SURFACE LOW MAY WRAP SLIGHTLY HIGHER DEWPOINTS WESTWARD AND CONTRIBUTE TO CONVECTIVE INITIATION BY EARLY AFTERNOON. STRONG HEATING AND COOL TEMPERATURES ALOFT WILL PROVIDE STEEP LAPSE RATES AND A RISK OF HAIL IN STRONGER CELLS. BY LATE AFTERNOON...MORE INTENSE STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO FORM NEAR THE DRYLINE WITH A CONTINUED RISK OF LARGE HAIL AND PERHAPS AN ISOLATED TORNADO. THREAT SHOULD SPREAD INTO WESTERN KS DURING THE EVENING BEFORE WEAKENING AFTER DARK.

sections.title: OK/TX PANHANDLES INTO SOUTHWEST TX
sections.text: STRONG HEATING OVER EASTERN NM AND WEST TX WILL HELP INTENSIFY THE DRYLINE LATER THIS AFTERNOON...PROVIDING THE FOCUS FOR WIDELY SCATTERED SEVERE STORMS. MESOSCALE MODEL GUIDANCE IS IN FAIR AGREEMENT OF STORMS BY 00Z FROM SOUTHEAST CO TO SOUTH OF AMA...WITH DEVELOPMENT SOUTHWARD ALONG DRYLINE DURING THE EVENING. FORECAST SOUNDINGS ALONG THIS ENTIRE AXIS WILL SUPPORT A RISK OF LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS. THOSE STORMS THAT CAN REMAIN DISCRETE MAY ALSO POSE A RISK FOR ISOLATED TORNADOES. STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO ORGANIZE UPSCALE INTO A LINEAR MCS BY 06Z AND PROPAGATE SOUTHEASTWARD TOWARD THE HILL COUNTRY. ..HART/GARNER.. 04/16/2009

sections.title: SRN PLAINS
sections.text: SCATTERED SUPERCELLS THAT DEVELOPED ALONG DIFFERENTIAL HEATING BOUNDARY CONTINUES OVER WRN TX BETWEEN MIDLAND AND AMARILLO WHERE THE ATMOSPHERE REMAINS MODERATELY UNSTABLE. STORMS HAVE BEEN MOVING NEWD OVER TOP OF THE WWD RETREATING CONVECTIVELY ENHANCED BOUNDARY WHERE LOW LEVEL HODOGRAPHS ARE AUGMENTED BY BACKED FLOW IN THE 0-1 KM LAYER. THREAT FOR LOW LEVEL MESOCYCLONES...LARGE HAIL AND ISOLATED TORNADOES WILL LIKELY PERSIST NEXT COUPLE HOURS OVER WRN TX AS SUPERCELLS INTERACT WITH THIS BOUNDARY. SATELLITE AND OBJECTIVE ANALYSIS DATA INDICATE A VORT MAX ROTATING NEWD THROUGH ERN NM INTO WRN TX ALONG SERN PERIPHERY OF UPPER LOW. AS THIS FEATURE CONTINUES NEWD...THE PACIFIC FRONT WILL MERGE WITH THE RETREATING DRYLINE AND CONTINUE EAST THROUGH WRN TX. ENHANCED LIFT RESULTING FROM THE MERGING BOUNDARIES AND DEEP LAYER FORCING FOR ASCENT ATTENDING THE NEWD EJECTING VORT MAX WILL LIKELY CONTRIBUTE TO DEVELOPMENT OF ADDITIONAL STORMS WHICH MAY GROW UPSCALE INTO AN MCS LATER THIS EVENING. ACTIVITY WILL REMAIN EMBEDDED WITHIN FAVORABLE VERTICAL SHEAR FOR ORGANIZED STORM STRUCTURES AND MAY CONTINUE TO POSE A THREAT FOR MAINLY LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND. LATER TONIGHT...STRONGEST STORMS

sections.title: RIO GRANDE AREA OF SW TX
ERN CO THROUGH SW KS
sections.text: DRYLINE OVER WRN TX ARCS NWWD TO A WEAK SURFACE LOW IN SE CO. LOW LEVEL MOISTURE AND INSTABILITY ARE MORE LIMITED IN THIS REGION WITH DEWPOINTS ONLY IN THE 40S AND MLCAPE AOB 500 J/KG EAST AND NE OF DRYLINE. STORMS WILL LIKELY CONTINUE DEVELOPING NWD INTO THIS AREA NEXT FEW HOURS. BULK SHEAR OF 40-50 KT WILL SUPPORT A THREAT FOR ORGANIZED STORMS WITH ISOLATED DAMAGING WIND AND HAIL POSSIBLE. HOWEVER...THE MARGINAL THERMODYNAMIC ENVIRONMENT WILL REMAIN A LIMITING FACTOR FOR A MORE ROBUST SEVERE THREAT. SEVERE POTENTIAL SHOULD DIMINISH IN THIS AREA LATER THIS EVENING AS THE BOUNDARY LAYER STABILIZES. ..DIAL.. 04/17/2009
